text:
maya: Customer Cobalt (org 3421) reported a p99 spike and slow writes starting ~02:10 UTC. Support ticket INC-3421 opened. Anyone oncall?

support-bot: Ticket INC-3421 created by maya and linked to customer Cobalt. Priority: P2. Assignee: unassigned.

oliver: I'm available, jumping in. @sasha can you grab a replica to profile? can we get kvcache hit rates and batching stats?

maya: attaching quick flamegraph and small log sample: https://internal.artifacts/reports/3421/flame.svg

maya: sample logs:
```
[2026-03-15T02:12:03Z] write-handler idx=7 dur_ms=182 p99=342
[2026-03-15T02:12:04Z] kvcache.hit=false key=abc user=co42
[2026-03-15T02:12:05Z] batch.size=1 timeout_ms=8
```

sasha: grabbing rnode-7 now, running perf: 
```
ssh rnode-7
sudo perf top -p $(pidof redwood-runtime)
# also dumping /proc/1/smaps for mem spikes
```

casey: FYI we shipped rollout 2026-03-15T01:40:00 that increased default `batch_timeout` to 8ms and enabled `async_write_coalesce=true` for dedicated nodes.

raj: that rollout also adjusted kvcache eviction heuristics (PR #2148). pushing a revert could help narrow root cause.

oliver: rolling back canary to previous batching config (batch_timeout:4ms) on canary group now — monitoring metrics.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] rollback initiated for rollout 2026-03-15_0140 by oliver. 3/3 canary pods updated.

sasha: initial perf shows elevated syscall time in the write path; stack samples point at poll()/epoll_wait spikes. collecting `strace` and `iostat` dumps.

maya: can you paste p99s after the rollback? customer has a call in ~25m.

oliver: quick numbers: p50 ~60ms (stable), p99 dropped from ~480ms -> ~210ms after canary rollback. still above baseline (~170ms).

casey: re-opening PR to revert `async_write_coalesce` for dedicated pools. @raj can you help run the patch on staging and sanity-check?

raj: on it. will run e2e on staging and report back by EOD.

maya: thanks all — please leave short updates here. I'll update the support ticket and join the customer call once we confirm steady p99 < 200ms. :thumbsup:
